description_en: A stone fountain from the 14th-15th centuryThe fountain is built on the eastern fringe of the village of Mānmā, 1 km south and down the hill of Mānmā-Khām̐ḍācakra, the Kalikot district headquarters.The fountain consists of a central panel carved with pilasters and a horizontal frieze ofāmalakamotifs and other geomatric patterns. Water is dispensed via two stylizedmakaraheads. Themakaraon the right spout is partly broken. PVC pipes have been insrted in both spouts. Each side of the central panel has a small platform. The side platforms are also faced with carved panels.Cement has been applied in areas were the stone facings were damaged.Similar fountains, known locally asmugrāhā, can be found throughout the region (Andolfatto 2019: 101-102). The fountain is located in the heartland of the Rāskoṭi kingdom. This dynasty ruled between the end of the 14th century and the end of the 18th century. Based on comparative analysis, the monument can be dated from circa 14th-15th century.
monument_assessment: Repaired , Surface damages, Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths)
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université.
